posts.title: Eleven weeks, one thermos
posts.excerpt: A long-stay family room, and what one steel thermos carried through eleven weeks.
posts.content:
My father spent eleven weeks on a cardiac ward at Calder Teaching Hospital, and for most of them I slept in a chair beside him. What I remember is the thermos: filled at five, carried across the car park, empty by seven.

When we opened the house in 2014 I wanted that thermos to have a kitchen that was already warm. Tobias unlocks it at 04:50 every day, and the long-stay families are usually the first ones in.

If your stay stretches past a week, ask for the long-stay rate: 20 % off every night, in any room. Nobody should have to count nights as well as hours.

posts.title: Arriving after the desk closes
posts.excerpt: How the key box and the night phone work when you get here after 21:00.
posts.content:
The front desk closes at 21:00, but the house does not. If you are on a late train or leaving a ward after visiting hours, phone +00 44 555 0142 and Rafael will answer, any hour until 07:00.

He will text you a code for the key box beside the front door. Inside is your room key and a card with the way to your room; the stairs are lit and the kitchen is stocked with tea.

Please keep your voice down on the landing: quiet hours run 22:00–06:00.

posts.title: Bunks, crayons and a quiet hour
posts.excerpt: Siblings staying with us while a child is on the ward.
posts.content:
Children under 4 stay free, and the family rooms have a wooden bunk that brothers and sisters tend to argue over for exactly one night.

Hannah keeps a low table in the kitchen with crayons and paper. Between 11:00 and 12:00 the house is hushed for carers who were up all night, so that is when the drawing happens.

If your child is on the ward and your other children are with you, tell us when you ask for a bed. We will put you near the kitchen and away from the stairs.
